themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 5 this week versus 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 3900% surge (z-score 14.74)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors, enforcement gaps, or organized street vending activity emerging in Greenpoint/Williamsburg this week.
evidence: 5 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 14.74 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY and DOH about what triggered vendor influx; are licenses being denied or ignored?
Check if new food hall, market, or event is driving vendor clustering in specific neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Drug & Public Drinking Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 5 this week versus 1.5 weekly average (233% spike, z-score 7.0), while public drinking complaints hit 4 this week versus 0.4 baseline (967% spike, z-score 7.49), plus park rule violations also at 4 complaints—suggesting a concentrated pattern of open-air substance use and disorder in parks or public spaces THIS WEEK.
evidence: Drug activity: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.5 weekly average (233% increase, z-score 7.0)
Public drinking: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 7.49)
Park rule violations: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 7.49)
Three converging indicators suggest organized or concentrated activity in shared public spaces
reporting_angles: Identify which parks/public spaces are complaint hotspots; interview residents and Parks Enforcement
Talk to advocacy groups and service providers about whether there's been a visible change in street activity or displacement from other neighborhoods
Investigate NYPD enforcement patterns and whether recent policy changes affect open-air use complaints

themes_detail.label: Animal-in-Park Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Animal in a park complaints surged to 29 this week versus 7.5 weekly average—a 287% increase (z-score 6.64)—indicating a sudden emergence of loose animals, wildlife conflicts, or off-leash enforcement gaps affecting public park safety THIS WEEK.
evidence: 29 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs 7.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Highest absolute complaint count among all current spikes
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Enforcement to determine which animals, which parks, and what trigger caused the spike (rabid animal sighting, dog pack, coyote, rats?)
Interview park regulars and dog owners about visible changes in animal behavior or leash compliance enforcement

themes_detail.label: Electrical Hazard Reports
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints rose to 5 last week versus 0.9 weekly average—a 471% increase (z-score 5.28)—suggesting possible downed lines, transformer failures, or exposed wiring creating infrastructure and safety risks in the district last week.
evidence: 5 electrical complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Electrical issues carry fire and electrocution risk
reporting_angles: Contact ConEd to determine if there were outages, equipment failures, or maintenance work in Greenpoint/Williamsburg last week
Check DOB records for related complaints, construction incidents, or emergency calls

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Spike (Recent)
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints peaked at 12 three weeks ago versus 0.8 weekly average—a 1500% spike (z-score 6.86)—though not THIS WEEK, this signal remains noteworthy as an indicator of recent disorder or possible upcoming seasonal recurrence heading into summer months.
evidence: 12 illegal fireworks complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 0.8 weekly average
Signal is aging but may recur as warmer weather approaches
reporting_angles: Check if fireworks spike was localized to specific neighborhoods; interview residents on causes (celebration, gang activity, copycat behavior)
Assess NYPD enforcement capacity and whether seizures occurred; monitor for recurrence
